name: hurst_exponent_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the Hurst exponent of the 10-minute (120-bar at 5s) log-return series distinguishes two distinct microstructure states: when H > 0.55, large institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms are executing directional orders, and each 5-second bar absorbs part of that flow — consecutive bars are autocorrelated, creating exploitable momentum over 30-90 seconds. When H < 0.45, NIFTY is oscillating between resting buy and sell limit orders as market makers quote both sides; at this point Bollinger Band touches reliably signal a 30-60 second bounce as those resting orders absorb the directional flow and price reverts. The regime switch is computed over 120 bars to filter noise while remaining responsive to the current session's microstructure — a 5-minute window is too short for reliable Hurst estimation (high variance), while a 30-minute window is too slow to adapt to mid-session regime changes.

indicators.name: hurst_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling Hurst exponent. NOT 12x-scaled from original's 60 1-min bars (which would give 720 bars = 60 min — too slow). Instead: 120 bars = 10 min is the shortest window that gives statistically meaningful R/S estimates (variance of Hurst estimator drops sharply with more data) while adapting to intraday regime shifts. Serves as a CONTEXT FILTER, not a trade trigger, consistent with the 10.3 framework for non-trigger indicators.

indicators.name: ema_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute fast EMA for trend entry in persistent regime. Compressed from original's EMA(8) on 1-min bars because at 5s we need a faster trigger — the 1-min EMA captures the same short-term momentum idea but adapted to our 5s bar resolution.

indicators.name: ema_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute slow EMA for trend direction in persistent regime. Compressed from original's EMA(20) on 1-min bars (20 min) — 36 bars = 3 min is the appropriate slow EMA for confirming that a micro-trend is sustained across multiple 5s bars.

indicators.name: bb_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute Bollinger Bands for mean-reversion entries in anti-persistent regime. Compressed from original's BB(20) on 1-min bars (20 min). At 5s bars, a 24-bar (2-min) BB captures the short oscillation cycle relevant for our 30-120s hold. Original's 20-min BB would be far too wide relative to our hold time.

indicators.name: ret_1
indicators.purpose: Single-bar return for direction confirmation in trending regime — ensures we enter in the direction of the current bar's momentum, not against it.

conditions: TRENDING: hurst_120 > 0.55 AND ema_12 > ema_36 AND ret_1 > 0
MEAN-REVERTING: hurst_120 < 0.45 AND close < bb_lower (oversold bounce)
buy_ce.confirmation: hurst_120 must be computed (at least 120 bars of session data available)

conditions: TRENDING: hurst_120 > 0.55 AND ema_12 < ema_36 AND ret_1 < 0
MEAN-REVERTING: hurst_120 < 0.45 AND close > bb_upper (overbought fade)
buy_pe.confirmation: hurst_120 must be computed (at least 120 bars of session data available)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 points because a NIFTY 5-10 second momentum burst that stalls and reverses past 8 spot points (4 option points at delta ~0.5) signals the institutional flow has absorbed — the Hurst regime signal is wrong and we should exit. Tight enough to protect capital in the fast 5s environment.
exit.target_rationale: 6 points captures ~40% of a typical NIFTY 30-90s momentum continuation (15-20 spot pts in a persistent regime) or ~60% of a mean-reversion bounce from a BB extreme (10-12 spot pts). At 1:1.5 R:R and expected 54% win rate, this is profitable after costs.

filters.vix_filter: None — VIX not used; Hurst exponent itself implicitly captures volatility regime
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 120 bars from 09:20 open for valid Hurst estimate) or after 15:25
filters.volume_filter: None — index volume is noisy at 5s; Hurst computation uses returns, not volume
filters.trend_filter: Hurst exponent itself IS the regime classifier; no separate trend filter needed
filters.spread_filter: Not applicable — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — Hurst exponent regime classification is not widely implemented at 5s intraday frequency; computational complexity deters most participants

adaptation_notes: Original traded NIFTY50 constituent stocks at 1-min bars with 60-bar Hurst window. Key changes: (1) Moved to NIFTY INDEX — eliminates stock-specific noise and uses the cleaner index price series where Hurst estimation is more reliable. (2) Hurst window: 120 bars (10 min) instead of scaling original's 60 min — 120 bars gives better statistical reliability than 60 bars while being short enough to track intraday regime shifts. (3) Entry indicators compressed to 5s scale: EMA(8/20 min) → EMA(1/3 min); BB(20 min) → BB(2 min). (4) Hold time compressed from 15-45 min to 30-120 seconds; stops/targets recalibrated to 5s option move magnitudes. (5) VWAP filter dropped — at 5s bars, VWAP confirmation would add too much lag; Hurst regime + EMA direction is sufficient.
weaknesses: R/S Hurst estimator has high variance on 120 bars — estimates can be noisy, causing false regime signals
Hurst computation is O(n × window) — the loop may be slow in pure Python for large datasets, though acceptable in this pipeline
Regime transitions (H shifting from >0.55 to <0.45) can happen abruptly mid-session, causing whipsaws at the boundary
Anti-persistent regime (H<0.45) BB signals require price to reach extremes — may generate few signals in quiet sessions
